relations.myth: Visitation and gift of the pipe
relations.note: The Buffalo Nation sends her as its representative to bring the sacred pipe.
relations.source: Lone Man in Densmore, Teton Sioux Music

relations.myth: Visitation and gift of the pipe
relations.note: Her divinely authorized mission brings the pipe and its teachings to the people.
Through her pipe, offerings and prayers are directed toward Wakȟáŋ Tȟáŋka.
relations.source: Black Elk and Brown, The Sacred Pipe

relations.myth: Wohpe and the Gift of the Pipe
relations.note: Walker-associated Oglala tradition identifies or conflates her with the female pipe mediator Wóȟpe.
One Walker-system genealogy makes Wóȟpe Skan’s daughter, applying here only through their disputed identification.
A Walker-system variant makes Wóȟpe Skan’s specially created mediator, conditionally extending this relation to Ptesan Win.
A Walker-associated genealogy names Sun as Wóȟpe’s parent, applying only under the disputed identification.
A Walker-associated genealogy names Moon as Wóȟpe’s parent, applying only under the disputed identification.
Wóȟpe chooses or marries South Wind; this applies to Ptesan Win only through their disputed identification.
relations.source: Walker narratives; Dooling, The Sons of the Wind
